Handle Duplicate AST Results

Source: R/prep_ast.R
prep_deduplicate_ast.Rd

Deduplicates AST records in two sequential steps:

  1. Exact-duplicate removal: drops rows that are fully identical across every key column plus the value column (e.g. patient + organism + antibiotic + date + value). These are true redundant records with no ambiguity.

  2. Conflict resolution: handles the remaining cases where the same key group has different values – by construction, every group with more than one row left after step 1 is a genuine conflict (same key, different value), never an unresolved exact duplicate.

Usage

prep_deduplicate_ast(
  data,
  mode = c("detect", "remove"),
  strategy = c("resistant_wins", "susceptible_wins", "first", "error", "drop_conflicts"),
  group_col = NULL,
  patient_col = "patient_id",
  organism_col = "organism_normalized",
  antibiotic_col = "antibiotic_normalized",
  date_col = "culture_date",
  ast_col = "ast_value_harmonized",
  return_diagnostics = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with AST data in long format.

mode

Character. "detect" (flag only) or "remove" (flag then resolve). Default "detect".

strategy

Character. Resolution strategy used only when mode = "remove". "resistant_wins" (default) and "susceptible_wins" pick one row per key group by clinical priority; "first" keeps whichever row came first (only appropriate once a caller has verified row order is meaningful or doesn't matter); "error" stops instead of resolving – a conflicting duplicate is never silently resolved by taking the first row or any priority order unless that policy was explicitly chosen; use this when a conflict should always be surfaced, not quietly picked for you. "drop_conflicts" removes every row belonging to a conflicting key group entirely (never guesses which value is right) – the surviving data has zero rows for that key, rather than one unverified row.

group_col

Character or NULL. Additional stratum identifier (e.g. hospital) included in the key when supplied, so that a patient/organism/antibiotic/date combination that legitimately recurs in two different strata (e.g. a hospital-local patient id reused at a different hospital) is never treated as one conflicting record. Default NULL (key is patient/organism/antibiotic/date only, as before).

patient_col

Character. Patient (or event) ID column. Default "patient_id".

organism_col

Character or NULL. Organism column; NULL drops it from the key (e.g. when the data has already been subset to one organism). Default "organism_normalized".

antibiotic_col

Character. Antibiotic (or antibiotic-class) column. Default "antibiotic_normalized".

date_col

Character or NULL. Culture date column; NULL drops it from the key (e.g. when date has already been folded into an event id upstream). Default "culture_date".

ast_col

Character. Harmonized AST value column. Default "ast_value_harmonized".

return_diagnostics

Logical. When TRUE, return a list with data (the usual return value), exact_duplicates_removed (the rows dropped in step 1, with their key columns, for a caller that needs its own per-key-group tally), and conflict_groups (the conflict summary data frame, one row per conflicting key group). Default FALSE (return just the data frame, as before).

Value

  • mode = "detect": original data with is_ast_duplicate logical column added.

  • mode = "remove": data with conflicts resolved (one row per key, or zero rows for a key group dropped by strategy = "drop_conflicts") and no flag column.

When return_diagnostics = TRUE, either of the above is wrapped as $data in the list described above.

Details

The key is c(group_col, patient_col, organism_col, antibiotic_col, date_col), with group_col/organism_col/date_col dropped from the key when NULL – lets this function key on exactly the columns a given caller's data actually has (e.g. a hospital/stratum identifier via group_col when patient/event ids are not already globally unique across strata, or no organism_col/date_col at all once that information is already folded into an event id upstream).

"detect"

After exact-dedup, flags conflicting rows with is_ast_duplicate = TRUE and prints a QC summary. Returns the data with the flag column so you can inspect before deciding how to resolve.

"remove"

Runs both steps: removes exact duplicates, then applies strategy to resolve any remaining conflicts.
